Front: What problem does Docker solve?
Back: Docker addresses the "Matrix from Hell" - compatibility issues between different application components their dependencies and the underlying operating system.

Front: What are the key problems in the "Matrix from Hell" scenario?
Back: Setting up end-to-end application stacks with multiple technologies compatibility issues with OS versions dependency conflicts (one service needs library v1 another needs v2) architecture changes requiring compatibility re-checks difficult developer onboarding with complex setup instructions and environment differences between development test and production.

Front: How does Docker solve the "Matrix from Hell" problem?
Back: Each component runs in a separate container with its own dependencies all containers share the same VM and OS but have isolated environments one-time Docker configuration with simple docker run command for all developers and consistent behavior across all environments.

Front: What are the layers in Docker container architecture from top to bottom?
Back: Application + Dependencies Container Layer (writable) Docker Image Layers (read-only) Docker Engine Operating System Hardware Infrastructure.

Front: What are the layers in Virtual Machine architecture from top to bottom?
Back: Application + Dependencies Guest Operating System (full OS) Hypervisor (ESX Hyper-V) Host Operating System Hardware Infrastructure.

Front: What is the size difference between containers and virtual machines?
Back: Containers are in megabytes while virtual machines are in gigabytes.

Front: What is the startup time difference between containers and virtual machines?
Back: Containers start in seconds while virtual machines start in minutes.

Front: How does resource usage differ between containers and virtual machines?
Back: Containers are lightweight with shared kernel while VMs are heavy with full OS per VM.

Front: How does isolation differ between containers and virtual machines?
Back: Containers provide process-level isolation with shared kernel while VMs provide complete isolation with separate kernels.

Front: What is the OS compatibility constraint for containers vs VMs?
Back: Containers must match host kernel (Linux containers on Linux) while VMs can run different OS types.

Front: What critical limitation do containers have regarding the OS kernel?
Back: Containers share the underlying OS kernel - Linux containers require a Linux kernel Windows containers require a Windows kernel and you cannot run Windows containers on a Linux host without a Windows VM.

Front: What are containers?
Back: Containers are completely isolated environments with their own processes network interfaces and mounts but they all share the same OS kernel.

What is Docker's role in containerization?
Back: Docker utilizes LXC containers but provides a high-level interface with powerful functionalities making containers easy to use.

Back: They all use the Linux kernel - the difference is in the software layer above the kernel.
